subject: general
question: A lent ₹10,000 to B for 3 years on compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually. C lent the same amount for the same period to D at 11% simple interest. Who gained more at the end of 3 years and how much?
solution:
**Given:**

A lent Rs10,000 to B for 3 years on compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually.

 C lent the same amount for the same period to D at 11% simple interest.

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = [Principal (P) × Rate of interest (R) × Time(T)] / 100

Compound interest = P(1+R/100)ⁿ - P [P= Principal , R= rate of interest]

Amount = Principal + Interest

**Calculation:**

After 3 years in compound interest, A earned

10000 ( 1 + 10/100)³ - 10000

⇒ 13310 - 10000 

⇒ Rs 3310

After 3 years in simple interest C earned,

(10000 × 11 × 3) / 100

⇒ Rs 3300

So A earned Rs (3310 - 3300) = Rs 10 more.

**A gained Rs10 more.**
